newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea said to hold 77,000T rice tender in June.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea said to hold 77,000T rice tender in June.

text.p: South Korea is expected to hold a tender at the end of June to buy 77,000 tonnes of rice to meet its 1997 quota under the World Trade Organisation (WTO), a report by Seoul-based U.S. agricultural officials said.
The report did not include tender details such as whether South Korea would seek long or medium grain rice.

The tendered rice would probably be imported well before South Korea's presidential elections, tentatively set for December 18, but after the Korean monsoon season from late June through July, the report said.
Initial indications from the South Korean government were that the tender would be held during the first quarter of this year for both political and economic reasons , the report said.

However, the tender was postponed, it said, apparently because of a series of domestic political events. Indications now are that the tender would not take place until after the local planting season, which typically runs until mid-June.

Officials at the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry were believed to be concerned that any tender held during the planting season would lead some farmers to reduce their planted area, the report said.
This would run counter to the agriculture ministry's efforts to maintain planted rice paddies at the targeted level of 1.045 million hectares.
South Korea imported 51,000 tonnes of long grain rice from India in 1995 and 64,000 tonnes of medium grain rice from China to meet its Minimum Market Access commitments in the WTO.

Most of South Korea's imported rice remains in storage, while 17,000 tonnes of Indian long grain rice has been processed by manufacturers of "makkoli", a traditional fermented rice wine, the report said.
